name: Identity for AI Agents

card.question: Can we trust who the agent is acting as?
card.title: Identity for AI agents: workloads, agents and the people they act for
card.description: Service principals, managed identities and AI agents as identities: an owner, no long-lived secrets, and runtime risk that inherits the trust of the person they act for. Mapped to Entra, SailPoint and Okta. Start with Part 1.
card.audience: Identity and security architects, IAM and IGA teams, and the risk owners who have to sign off on AI agents acting with real permissions.

inShort.1: A privileged role without MFA should be blocked, but an agent can’t answer an MFA prompt, so that rule would block every automation you run. Non-human identities need their own baseline, an accountable owner, no long-lived secrets, and a risk score that inherits the risk of the person they act for.

1.title: Microsoft Entra: Owners, sponsors and managers for agents

excerpts.1: “Privileged role, no MFA: block” is a good rule for people. Applied to a workload, it blocks every automation you run. How to score service principals, managed identities and AI agents, including the trust of the person an agent acts for.
